extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO OED staff, and attorneys subject to USPTO disciplinary rules
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, rules, and procedural requirements governing disciplinary proceedings and sanctions for practitioners registered to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office (including applicable statutory/regulatory bases, misconduct definitions, mitigation factors, and ordered sanctions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction of the USPTO Director
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.19.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites these statutory and regulatory provisions as the basis for the Office's authority to approve settlement agreements and impose discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility and Rules of Professional Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is subject to the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility or the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct; the Code applies to conduct prior to May 3, 2013 and the Rules apply to conduct on or after May 3, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners' conduct is evaluated under the version of the USPTO ethics rules that was in effect when the conduct occurred. See 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.20-10.112 (Code) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101-11.901 (Rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proscribed dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct that involves dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation violates USPTO professional responsibility rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent acknowledged that copying and retaining confidential employer data knowing he was not authorized to possess it supports a finding of dishonesty under § 10.23(b)(4). Such misconduct is a basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to deliver client property on withdrawal (37 C.F.R. § 10.40(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must deliver to the client all property to which the client is entitled upon withdrawing from employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to return client property (e.g., confidential information belonging to an employer/client) constitutes a violation; the Indiana proceedings found a violation of Rule 1.16(d) and the USPTO found § 10.40(a) applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition/consideration of prior public discipline by a State (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Being publicly disciplined on ethical or professional misconduct grounds by a duly constituted authority of a State is proscribed/considered under the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A state public disciplinary action may be the basis for USPTO action; the Final Order cites § 11.804(h) as violated due to the Indiana Supreme Court suspension and related stipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 upon suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner who ceases practice related to the Office must comply with the duties and procedures set out in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent voluntarily ceased all activities related to practice before the Office and complied with § 11.58 on or before December 22, 2014; compliance includes notification and other administrative steps required when practice is suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement petition process under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: A suspended practitioner remains suspended until the OED Director grants a petition requesting reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly conditions return to practice on the OED Director's grant of a § 11.60 petition; practitioners must follow the procedural and substantive requirements of § 11.60 to seek reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, including electronically publishing the Final Order in the OED's FOIA Reading Room and publishing a notice in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order mandates prompt dissipation of disciplinary information to the public record (FOIA reading room and Official Gazette) and provides model language for a Notice of Suspension materially consistent with the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions imposed for the stipulated misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters for ninety (90) days commencing nunc pro tunc on December 22, 2014, and related administrative restrictions are imposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific measures ordered include: (i) dissociation of Respondent's name from all USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates; (ii) prohibition on applying for or obtaining a USPTO Customer Number or PKI certificate until reinstatement; (iii) remaining suspended until OED grants a petition under § 11.60; (iv) publication of the Final Order and Notice of Suspension. These are the concrete sanctions used to effect discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of prior conduct as aggravating factor in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or the Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding in future complaints or proceedings concerning similar misconduct, including as an aggravating factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states the record may be used (1) when addressing further complaints of same or similar misconduct and (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding either as an aggravating factor in determining discipline or to rebut statements by Respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors considered in the agreed resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors reflected in the agreed resolution include: (i) no prior disciplinary history before the Office during nearly 24 years of registration; (ii) Respondent represented he had no intent to harm the client; (iii) Respondent returned the confidential information to the client upon request and did not intend to share it with third parties; and (iv) Respondent fully cooperated with OED during investigation and resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These mitigating considerations were explicitly listed in the Notice of Suspension as factors influencing the negotiated resolution and the length/character of imposed sanctions. The stipulation also included Respondent's belief that information was public or would become public and that breach of employment agreement was not intentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement approval and procedural basis (37 C.F.R. § 11.26 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: The parties submitted a Proposed Settlement of Disciplinary Matter pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.26 to the Under Secretary/Director for approval, and the action results from settlement under the cited statutory/regulatory authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agreement resolved all disciplinary action by the USPTO arising from the stipulated facts and required approval by the Director; the Order references the statutory/regulatory framework (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D), 32; 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.26, 11.59) governing settlement, approval, and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs in disciplinary settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the Agreement and the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement explicitly apportions no award of costs between the parties; each is responsible for its own expenses related to the investigation, settlement, and implementation.
